market_preferred_note: Same framing as round 1: investors preferred Kilicdaroglu/orthodox policy (Erdogan's first-round lead hit lira/bonds): https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2023-05-12/rpt-investors-buckle-pivotal-turkey-elections
notes: Run-off. POLITICO aggregate 'last updated 28 May' per Wikipedia. odds_date = article last-updated date. Official national total (no diaspora split).

poll_basis: no verifiable final nationwide local-vote poll found (Wikipedia lists only city-level polls); poll columns left blank
notes: Actual = national municipal-councillor vote share (Wikipedia/YSK). Without a verified final nationwide poll, cand_a=AKP is assigned as the incumbent national leader (AKP led the 2019 local vote 42.56 vs 29.36) - this ordering is NOT poll-based; margin negative because CHP came first (first CHP national win since 1977). market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: mean of 2 polls: Ipsos Markinor (ANC 64.7, DA 10.8; 9.1% unsure excluded and renormalised) and Plus 94 (ANC 60, DA 16; as reported)
notes: National Assembly ballot. results_known = 23 Apr 2009, when partial IEC results showed ANC victory in sight (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2009/4/23/anc-nears-s-africa-election-win); IEC final results 25 Apr 2009 (sanews). Markinor fieldwork was early March 2009 (Politicsweb 15 Apr) and Plus 94 fieldwork date not reported; poll_date is the Wikinews publication date. Wikinews gives Markinor undecided 4.2% + refused 3.9%, Politicsweb gives 9.1% unsure; Politicsweb figure used. No Wikipedia poll table exists for 2009. Polls are old/sparse - low confidence. market_preferred left blank: no clear-cut financial-press framing found (ANC win never in doubt).

poll_basis: final Ipsos/Sunday Times poll (Apr 2014, published 4 May 2014); undecided already allocated by pollster (no DK share reported)
notes: National Assembly ballot. results_known = 8 May 2014, ANC lead clear from IEC results board (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2014/5/8/south-africas-ruling-anc-takes-election-lead); IEC final results 10 May 2014. Only Ipsos published a regular series in the final weeks (a DA-internal Greenberg poll, ANC 59/DA 26, excluded as partisan). Wikipedia notes the final Ipsos wave was based on 500 interviews on 23 Apr 2014. market_preferred blank: no clear-cut framing found.

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each main pollster: IRR 18-25 Apr (ANC 49.5, DA 21.3, DK 0.9) and Ipsos 22 Mar-17 Apr (ANC 56.9, DA 15.2, DK 12.5); each normalised excl. don't know
market_preferred_note: Investors wanted a strong ANC (Ramaphosa) mandate; weak ANC/coalitions seen as rand-negative: https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/314974/why-investors-want-a-big-win-for-the-anc/
notes: National Assembly ballot. results_known = 10 May 2019 (75% of districts declared, ANC 57.2%: https://businesstech.co.za/news/?p=315956); IEC declared final results 11 May 2019. Excluded Intellidex 2 May 'investor poll' (survey of investors' expectations, not voters). Coding: for SA, 'a' = strong ANC share (reform-wing Ramaphosa mandate), the financial-press framing in 2019.

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each pollster with fieldwork in final week: AtlasIntel 25-28 May, Social Research Foundation 27 May, Afrobarometer 22 May; shares as published (no DK column)
market_preferred_note: Not a/b-codable: markets favoured an ANC-DA (or ANC+MPC) coalition over ANC-EFF/MK; see https://poundsterlinglive.com/zar/20372-south-african-rand-rallies-investors-spy-potential-anc-da-coalition
notes: National Assembly ballot. ANC won plurality but lost its majority (40.18%) -> GNU with DA. results_known = 31 May 2024, when partial IEC count put ANC clearly below 50% (https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/liveblog/2024/5/31/south-africa-election-results-live-early-results-put-anc-short-of-majority); Reuters flagged likely loss of majority on 30 May; IEC declared final results 2 Jun 2024. Poll leader/winner by plurality = ANC, but the market-relevant outcome was ANC<50% and coalition partner choice; coding left blank deliberately. Afrobarometer 'others' column (22%) may contain undecided - not normalised (not separable).
